CLI reference

sitefile <command> --help prints the options of each command. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 an error (error[E_CODE]: message), 2 a usage error.

Building

sitefile build [context] [-f Sitefile] [-o out] [--format fmt] [-t name[:tag]]... [options]
sitefile validate [context] [--json]
sitefile inspect  [context] [--json]

build accepts these image-related options on top of the ones in the README:

| Option | Meaning | | --- | --- | | -t, --tag name[:tag] | also store the build as an image in the local store (repeatable). With -t and no -o, only the store is written and nothing is created in the context; with both, both happen. | | --format oci / -o x.oci.tar | write an OCI image: an OCI archive for a .tar destination, an OCI layout directory otherwise (dist.oci.tar by default) | | --base <image> | build the oci image on <image> (runnable; overrides EXPORT ... AS oci BASE); a bare name means Docker Hub. Pin it: nginx:alpine@sha256:... | | --insecure-registry host[:port] | allow plain http to that registry (repeatable) | | --oci-root /path | directory of the files inside the image layer (default /srv/www; overrides EXPORT ... AT) | | --platform os/arch | image platform metadata (default linux/amd64) | | --label key=value | add an OCI image config label (repeatable; overrides defaults such as org.opencontainers.image.title) | | --git-labels | add org.opencontainers.image.source/.revision from the git checkout. Off by default: they change the image ID on every commit, and finding the checkout reads outside the context. Credentials in remote URLs are dropped. |

build, validate and inspect also accept:

| Option | Meaning | | --- | --- | | --allow-exec name[=/abs/path] | allow a TOOL name (an external program) to run; repeatable. A bare name is looked up on PATH when the build starts and the resolved real path is printed (tool ffmpeg -> /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg). A TOOL that is not allowed fails with E_UNSUPPORTED naming the flag to add. The program runs with your privileges: allow only what you trust. | | --no-cache | do not read or write the TRANSFORM result cache for this build | | --plugin-timeout ms | per-call time limit for TRANSFORM plugins and tools (default 60000) |

Transform cache

TRANSFORM results (plugins and TOOLs) are cached in $SITEFILE_HOME/cache/transform (default ~/.sitefile/cache/transform), beside the image store but separate from it (image prune does not touch it). See PLUGINS.md.

sitefile cache info [--json]              location, entries, blobs, size
sitefile cache prune [--older-than days]  delete every cached result, or only entries unused for N days

Image store

The store lives in $SITEFILE_HOME, or ~/.sitefile. Tests and scripts should always set SITEFILE_HOME. It is an OCI image layout (image-spec v1.1):

$SITEFILE_HOME/
  oci-layout            {"imageLayoutVersion":"1.0.0"}
  index.json            image index; tags are entries annotated org.opencontainers.image.ref.name = "name:tag"
  blobs/sha256/<hex>    manifest, config and layer blobs (identical blobs are stored once)
  servers/<id>.json     site server state (see below)
  servers/<id>.log      site server log
  lock                  lock file held while the store is modified
  • An image is one manifest, one config and one layer. The layer is a deterministic tar.gz of the site's files under a root directory (/srv/www by default). See Export formats > oci in LANGUAGE.md. The image holds files only: it has no entrypoint and is not runnable on its own.
  • The image ID is the manifest digest (sha256:<hex>; shown as the first 12 hex digits). The same files, root, platform and labels give the same ID, so rebuilding identical output does not create a new image.
  • An image without a tag is dangling (an index.json entry without a ref name); it shows as <none>. Building a tag again with different content leaves the old image dangling until image prune.
  • index.json also records, per entry, dev.sitefile.created: when the image was first stored (bookkeeping only; it is not part of any digest, and is what CREATED shows).
  • Writes are temp file + rename; modifications hold the lock file (stale locks of dead processes are broken), so concurrent sitefile calls do not corrupt the index. Every blob is digest-checked when read; a mismatch, a missing blob or a bad diff_id is E_STORE. Build-arg values are never stored.

Reference grammar

[registry-host[:port]/]name[:tag][@sha256:<64 hex>]
name = component ('/' component)*      component = [a-z0-9]+([._-][a-z0-9]+)*
tag  = [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}        (default: latest)

The first path component is a registry host when it contains . or : or is localhost. References are validated everywhere (E_USAGE for a bad one). Locally a registry-qualified name is just a tag (sitefile tag blog:1 localhost:5000/blog:1), stored as registry/name:tag. Docker Hub aliases (docker.io, index.docker.io, registry-1.docker.io) are one registry (docker.io; its API host is registry-1.docker.io), and a Hub name without a namespace lives in library/. A name without a registry host defaults to Docker Hub only for pull and BASE (nginx:alpine is docker.io/library/nginx:alpine); everywhere else, and for push, it is a local name. A short image ID (12 to 64 hex digits, optionally sha256:-prefixed) resolves when it is unique.

Registries: push and pull

sitefile tag blog:1 localhost:5000/team/blog:1
sitefile push localhost:5000/team/blog:1
sitefile pull localhost:5000/team/blog:1          # or name@sha256:... ; nginx:alpine means Docker Hub
sitefile pull --platform linux/arm64 nginx:alpine

The client speaks the OCI distribution spec v1.1: a /v2/ probe, then Bearer-token auth (the WWW-Authenticate realm/service/scope; an anonymous token first for pulls, credentials when the registry rejects it, and straight away for pushes) or Basic auth.

  • push HEADs every blob and uploads only the missing ones (monolithic POST + PUT); layers of a BASE image are mounted from the base's repository when it is on the same registry; then the manifest is PUT and the digest the registry returns is checked against ours. The pushed manifest digest equals the local image ID.
  • pull accepts OCI and Docker v2 manifests and indexes/manifest lists (for an index the --platform variant, default linux/amd64), checks every blob's sha256 and size while streaming into a temp file (nothing unverified is ever stored), and a manifest fetched by digest must hash to it. The platform manifest is stored unchanged (its digest is the image ID) and tagged as written. Pulled third-party images are listed, pushed and used as BASE; only images built by sitefile can be served or saved as a site.
  • Limits: --max-download-bytes per blob (default 2 GiB), 8 GiB per image, 4 MiB per manifest or token response, --timeout idle time per request (default 30 s), 30 minutes per blob transfer.
  • Transport: https. Plain http only for loopback registries (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1) and hosts named with --insecure-registry host[:port] (repeatable; or $SITEFILE_INSECURE_REGISTRIES, comma separated); those try https first and fall back to http. The registry host itself may be a private address (you named it). Redirects (registries send blob downloads to a CDN) are followed manually, at most 5, each hop re-checked: a target on another origin must be https and have no credentials in its URL, and must resolve to public addresses (checked at connect time) unless --allow-private-network; the Authorization header is never sent to another origin. Token-endpoint realms obey the same rules. Compressed transfer encodings are refused.
  • Credentials, first match wins: --username with --password-stdin (never a password on the command line); $SITEFILE_REGISTRY_AUTH, a JSON object such as {"ghcr.io":"user:token","reg.example.com":{"username":"u","password":"p"}}; then the Docker config ($DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json, else ~/.docker/config.json): credHelpers[host], then auths[host] (auth base64 user:pass, username/password, or an identitytoken exchanged at the token endpoint), then credsStore. Docker Hub is found under docker.io, index.docker.io or https://index.docker.io/v1/. Credential helpers execute a program: only when the Docker config names one, as docker-credential-<name> get found on PATH (the name must be a plain word, no shell is involved), with the server address on stdin and nothing secret on argv. Credentials are fetched only when a registry asks for authentication, and tokens/passwords are kept in memory and never printed or put in an error message.
  • Errors: E_AUTH (credentials missing/rejected), E_NOT_FOUND (404), E_INTEGRITY (digest mismatch), E_TOO_LARGE, E_PROTOCOL/E_SSRF_BLOCKED (transport policy), E_REGISTRY (anything else the registry says).

To run a pushed or pulled site image, use it as COPY --from= source or serve it with sitefile serve; for a runnable container image, build on a base with BASE (see LANGUAGE.md). The default platform of images is linux/amd64 (reproducible, metadata only for files-only images); on an arm64 host Docker warns about the mismatch. Use --platform linux/arm64 to label them for arm64.

Commands

| Command | Description | | --- | --- | | images [--json] [--digests] [-q] | REPOSITORY TAG IMAGE ID CREATED FILES SIZE, one row per tag. --digests adds the full ID, -q prints short IDs only. Alias: image ls. | | image inspect <ref\|id> [--json] | ID, tags, platform, root, layer/config digests, labels, and the files (the layer is fully verified). | | tag <src> <dst> | add or move the local tag <dst> to image <src>. | | rmi [-f] <ref\|id>... | remove tags. The image leaves the index when no tag is left. An ID with several tags needs -f. Alias: image rm. | | image prune | drop untagged images, delete unreferenced blobs, print the space reclaimed. | | save <ref\|id> -o out [--format fmt] [--base-url url] [--force] | export an image. Formats as in build -o: a directory, .zip, .tar, .tar.gz/.tgz, .wbn; .oci.tar (or --format oci with a .tar destination) writes the stored image itself as an OCI archive, and --format oci with any other destination as an OCI layout directory (same digests as the store). A non-empty destination needs --force. | | image diff <a> <b> | A/D/C lines for added, removed and changed paths. |

Site servers

sitefile serve [--name n] [-p [host:]port] [-d] [--spa] <ref|id|./dir>
sitefile servers [-a] [--json]                   # also: sitefile server ls
sitefile server stop [--time secs] <name|id>...
sitefile server rm [-f] <name|id>...
sitefile server logs [-f] [-n lines] <name|id>
sitefile server restart <name|id>

servers lists NAME SITE URL STATUS ID, where SITE is the image reference or directory being served (--json calls it site).

serve serves an image from the store (the files under its root), or a directory (an argument starting with ./, ../ or /, or ending in /) read once at start through the sandboxed local reader: a symlink leaving the directory is an error, and hidden files (.git, .env, ... except .well-known) are not served.

  • Binds 127.0.0.1 and a free port unless -p is given. -p 8080, -p 127.0.0.1:8080, -p [::1]:8080. 0.0.0.0 (or ::) is bound only when you write it in -p (a warning is printed). A port in use is error[E_SERVER].
  • Foreground by default: prints the URL and one access-log line per request (GET /path 200 1234 1.2ms); Ctrl-C stops it. Foreground servers are not listed by servers; --name needs -d.
  • Behaviour: GET and HEAD only (405 with Allow otherwise); / and /dir/ serve index.html; /dir redirects (301) to /dir/; no directory listings; 404 with a small page; content-type from the extension; ETag is the file digest and If-None-Match gives 304; cache-control: no-cache; x-content-type-options: nosniff. Paths are percent-decoded per segment; .., an encoded /, NUL, control characters and backslashes are 400. --spa serves /index.html for unknown paths whose last segment has no file extension (a missing /app.js stays 404).
  • -d detaches. A server is tracked by $SITEFILE_HOME/servers/<id>.json (id, name, image, source, spa, requested bind, host, port, pid, started, logFile, ready) and <id>.log. serve -d writes the state, spawns a detached node serve-worker.js <id> with stdout/stderr on the log, and waits until the worker has recorded its pid and port (a failure to start is reported with the worker's error and leaves no entry). servers never trusts the file alone: running means the pid is alive and the port answers with this server's x-sitefile-server: <id> header; anything else shows as exited. IDs are 12 hex digits, names are unique (auto names look like site-1a2b3c).
  • stop sends SIGTERM, waits --time seconds (default 5), then SIGKILL; stopping an exited server is a no-op. rm refuses a running server unless -f. restart stops and starts it again with the same name and bind address, serving the same image ID (a directory is re-read). logs -f follows the log until Ctrl-C.
